_summary: Declares the Software project pack: artifacts, evidence, evidence command hints, review lenses, completion requirements, and tool probes for software projects.
name: Software
summary: The default pack for applications, services, libraries, and command-line tools. It expects a repository, builds, tests, and a first phase that installs, starts, and completes one real user action.

artifacts.name: Source code
artifacts.description: Application, library, or tool code in the repository.

artifacts.name: Tests
artifacts.description: Automated tests and the commands that run them.

artifacts.name: Documentation
artifacts.description: README, setup instructions, and user or developer documentation.

typical_stages: First working path: install, start, and complete one real user action

evidence.name: build
evidence.description: The project's build command exits successfully on the revision under review.

evidence.name: unit-tests
evidence.description: The project's automated test command exits successfully; new behavior and its failure paths have tests.

evidence.name: lint
evidence.description: The project's formatter, linter, or static analyzer reports no error.

evidence.name: dependency-audit
evidence.description: A dependency vulnerability check reports no unresolved high or critical finding, and every new dependency has a compatible license.

evidence.name: security-scan
evidence.description: A security scanner already used by the project reports no unresolved high finding; secrets are absent from the tree.

evidence.name: failure-handling-check
evidence.description: Invalid input, missing files, timeouts, interruption, and restart produce a clear error or a safe recovery instead of silent damage.

evidence.name: user-journey
evidence.description: A person installs or starts the software, completes the phase's main user action, and records the exact steps and result.

evidence.name: privacy-check
evidence.description: Personal data collected, stored, logged, or sent is listed and limited to what the task needs; logs and error output are redacted.

evidence.name: accessibility-check
evidence.description: User-facing screens, terminal output, and documentation are checked against WCAG 2.2 Level AA where applicable, including keyboard use and non-color status cues.

evidence.name: maintainability-review
evidence.description: New code has clear names, small functions, current comments, required file headers, and no unused flags or placeholder extension points.

evidence.name: documentation-check
evidence.description: Setup, usage, and help text match the behavior shipped in the phase, and every unavailable feature is marked as not yet available.

evidence.name: license-check
evidence.description: New dependencies and copied material are compatible with the project's license and carry their notices; changed files keep their headers.

evidence.name: release-check
evidence.description: A clean checkout installs, builds, and starts by following the documentation on the operating systems the project supports.

review_lenses.name: Correctness and reliability
review_lenses.focus: Behavior matches the accepted decisions and plan; failure handling, recovery, and edge cases are covered by evidence.

review_lenses.name: Security and privacy
review_lenses.focus: Input validation, command and query construction, permissions, credentials, personal data, and dependency risks.

review_lenses.name: Accessibility and user experience
review_lenses.focus: Keyboard use, labels, contrast, error messages, and plain-language output for user-facing surfaces.

review_lenses.name: Maintainability, documentation, licensing, and release readiness
review_lenses.focus: Readable code, current documentation, headers and notices, license compatibility, and packaging.

completion: Every required evidence item for the phase has a current record tied to the exact revision reviewed.
Both phase reviewers approved, or the user accepted a recorded reduced-assurance decision.
The plan revision reflects every accepted change, TODO, deviation, skipped check, and deferral.
The first phase installs, starts, and completes one real user action.
